sentence: This project uses collaboration to improve the diagnosis and treatment of cancer, focusing on targeted cancer therapeutics, cancer metabolism and the immune microenvironment.
This project studies how neural crest stem cells form, to reveal the genetic causes of craniofacial diseases.
This project examines how changes in physical activity patterns over time relate to preventing cardiovascular disease, using accelerometry data.
This project investigates how DNA damage response pathways affect the survival of retinal ganglion cells in traumatic optic neuropathy, a condition that causes vision loss.
This project designs proteins with a high refractive index and delivers them to living tissues, so optical microscopy can image deeper.
This project determines how the brain uses signals from the bladder to control urination.
This project studies methods for activating and controlling invariant Natural Killer T cells, a class of specialized lymphocytes, to develop immunotherapy of cancer.
This project develops machine learning techniques for clinical decision support in critical care that handle missingness and bias in clinical data.
This project develops tools to reveal molecular signatures of non-coding RNAs and their interactors in prostate cancer, comparing aggressive versus indolent prostate cancer.
This project studies how developing sperm and eggs exchange DNA through recombination events, which helps prevent infertility, miscarriages, birth defects and cancer.
This project studies prion-based behaviors of chromatin remodeling complexes in yeast and humans and how they cause transcriptomic modifications and phenotypes.
This project develops proteomics strategies to understand inflammation caused by environmental and external agents, and to identify potential drug targets.
This project studies how epigenetic mechanisms facilitate immune evasion in osteosarcoma, using a co-culture system and mouse models.
This project studies neuropsychiatric manifestations of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, including cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression and fatigue, using mice to model brain dysfunction.
This project tries to find out how excessive cellular stretch is transmitted by intracellular calcium signaling pathways.
This project develops a computational microscopy method that captures signals from fluorescent voltage-sensing reporter proteins to measure electrical neuronal activity in mammalian brain tissue.
This project tests whether fast-spiking interneurons in the nucleus accumbens modulate motivational behaviors that are disrupted in addiction to opioids.
This project develops a cancer model using patient-derived tumor organoids of head and neck cancer, screened with clinical radiotracers, to measure sensitivity to treatments.
This project tries to find out which mechanisms control the change from adaptive to chronic hypertrophy, an enlargement of the heart, in heart failure.
This project studies a processing step in the streptococcal ribosome, which may play a role in antibiotic resistance and survival under stress conditions.
